chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Kawkabi, from al-Amriki al-Khorasani, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:

In mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership), whatever he spends during his journey is deducted from the total capital, and when he returns to his town, whatever he spends is deducted from his share of the profit.

key_terms.الْمُضَارَبَةِ: Mudarabah, a profit-sharing partnership where one party provides capital and the other provides labor.
key_terms.سَفَرِهِ: His journey/travel, referring to the period the managing partner is away.
key_terms.نَصِيبِهِ: His share, referring to the portion of profit allocated to the managing partner.

ai.seo_question: How are travel and living expenses handled in a Shia mudarabah partnership?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the distribution of costs in a mudarabah contract, distinguishing between travel expenses deducted from the principal capital and post-arrival living expenses borne by the manager's profit share. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the capital provider bears the risk of the investment's initial mobilization, while the working partner assumes the cost of their sustenance during the active management phase, ensuring equitable risk-sharing.
